title: finding(ci): the coverage gate has been BLIND, not merely red, on the last three `main` commits — a 15s timeout in one shard means the thresholds were never evaluated
body:
Found by the `domain:ui` PM seat while ruling out a base-branch failure before handing two PR reds back to their seats. ⛔ Filed as a `finding` only; grading is the triage seat's.

## The claim

⭐ The coverage gate on `main` is not failing loudly — **it is blind**. Its thresholds have not been evaluated on the last three commits, and it says so itself.

## Measured — `main`, three consecutive merge commits

| commit | red checks |
|:--|:--|
| `383502b231` (objectui#9265) | `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard 1/4)` |
| `20b507aff0` (objectui#9258) | `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard 1/4)`, `Test (coverage shard 3/4)` |
| `a08096a11a` (objectui#9259) | `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard 1/4)` |

⚠️ The plain `Test (shard N/4)` lane is **green** on all three. This is the coverage lane only — which is exactly why it has been easy to read as background noise.

## The chain, in the gate's own words

`Test (coverage)`'s failing step is named **"Say out loud whether the coverage gate ran on this commit"**, and it reports:

> `shards=failure blobs=skipped merge=skipped report=skipped` — no complete merged report was produced for `383502b2319af9e4531ffd37f5cd76dd55e283e9`, so the **coverage thresholds were never evaluated on this commit**

The upstream cause is one timeout:

```
Test (coverage shard 1/4)  →  step "Run tests with coverage (shard 1/4)"
scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts:1603
  Error: Test timed out in 15000ms.
```

⇒ one shard dies on a 15s timeout → no blobs → no merge → no report → **the thresholds are skipped rather than failed**.

## ⭐ Why this is worse than an ordinary red

A threshold that is never evaluated does not report "coverage dropped". It reports nothing, and the surrounding job turns red for a reason that reads like infrastructure. So:

- coverage could have regressed arbitrarily far across these merges and **nothing would have said so**;
- the merge queue evidently does not gate on this lane — objectui#9265, objectui#9258 and objectui#9259 all landed while it was red — so the red is load-bearing on nobody and decays into wallpaper;
- ⛔ and the step that announces the skip is doing its job perfectly. The failure is not that the gate is silent; it is that **its announcement has no consumer**.

## ⚠️ What is NOT measured

- **How long this has been true.** Only three commits were read. ⛔ Do not assume it started there — the first commit where the report stopped being produced is the number that matters and it is unmeasured.
- **Whether the thresholds would pass if they ran.** Nothing here says coverage is bad; it says coverage is unknown. Those are different findings and this card claims only the second.
- **Whether the timeout is the only cause.** `Test (coverage shard 3/4)` was also red on `20b507aff0` and was not diagnosed; it may be the same timeout on a different shard or something else.
- **Why `check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts:1603` takes more than 15s**, and whether it is getting slower. That test scans the tree, so a corpus that grows over time is the obvious hypothesis — ⛔ untested, and "raise the timeout" is a repair for a symptom whose cause has not been read.

## What a repair has to decide

1. Fix or budget the timeout so the shards produce blobs. ⛔ But raising the number without reading why it grew is treating the reading, not the defect.
2. Decide whether "no merged report" should be a **hard failure that blocks the queue**, or stay advisory. Today it is neither: red, and blocking nothing.
3. If it stays advisory, then something has to consume the announcement — otherwise this recurs the moment it is fixed.

## Related

- objectui#9201, objectui#9126, objectui#8754, objectui#7844, objectui#7575 all touch `check-i18n-dead-keys`, but none of them is about its **runtime** or about the coverage report. Dedup ran over all 457 open issues with controls fired **both ways** — a `check-i18n-dead-keys` control returned 6, an impossible-string control returned 0 — and both target queries returned 0.
